execution_log.summary: Worker implemented P0 in the order the brief pins: a stubbed TFind skeleton (Create/Destroy real, paths/buildArgv/mapRc/byName answering `__TFIND_PENDING__` with rc 2), then 004/005/006 + tests.sh written against PLAN §3, then the tutil 001 registry cases, then the red run (tfind 170 FAIL of 215; tutil 001 9 FAIL of 74 — the critic's blocker 1 reproduced: `uV.argv TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES` was rc 0 and the registry came back as `(printf hello)`), then the implementation. tutil.sh: `declare -ga TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES=( __tu_ __tg_ __th_ __tt_ )` below the re-source guard, and `tutil._badOut` rewritten as reserved-name -> fail-closed -> `kk._outName NAME "${TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES[@]}"` -> the ${inst}_args/_argv/_paths case. The fail-closed test needs `${TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES@a}`, which is itself a nounset FAULT on an unset name or a plain scalar, so the frame does `local -; set +u` (options restored on return) — a fault is not a refusal. tfind.sh appends `__tfd_` only if absent and releases its two scratch globals. Two test corrections against the live tool, both reported: (1) the word scan means `addArg -name '-exec'` is refused with print0 = 1 (an action word used as a VALUE) — implemented per the plan's letter and now pinned as a documented over-refusal, with a separate case proving `-execute`/`-printx` are NOT refused; (2) 006's `[!-(]` guard tripped on the unit's own comment naming the wrong spelling, so the check now strips comment lines first. No deviation from the plan's letter anywhere else. Gate: tfind 216/216 on 5.2.37 and 5.3.9 (threaded) and 216/216 under --mode single on 5.2.37; tutil 197/197 on both bashes; tgrep 185/185, thead 182/182, ttail 200/200 on 5.2.37. Master sweep: run by reviewer. NOT committed, NOT pushed; P1 not started. REVIEW (supervisor, 2026-09-16): tfind 216/216 and tutil 197/197 reproduced on both bashes; probes on both bashes — argv shape with -print0 last, toArray 4 records incl. the newline name vs count 5 under -print, maxDepth 08 -> 8, type f,f = tool rc 1, print0 + -exec rc 2, a -bad start point rc 2, the registry refused as an out-name with 5 entries intact, byName in place and rc 2 without a path, partial failure keeps the record with rc 1. The registry refactor verified in tutil.sh: name refused, `local -; set +u` around the attribute probe, fail-closed on a non-array or empty registry. Master sweep 26/26 suites 0 [FAIL] on both bashes. Committed as kcl c281d40.

Opus critic, 18 probe scripts on both bashes (both are MSYS builds resolving their own root's find 4.10.0). BLOCKERS: (1) the TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES registry is itself a fillable out-name — `f.argv TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES` replaced it with the argv and every family prefix became fillable process-wide — and it fails OPEN when empty/unset (bash >= 4.4 does not fault "${arr[@]}" on an unset array under set -u) -> the registry name is refused in _badOut and an empty registry refuses every name; (2) print0 = 1 plus an action in the extras interleaves two actions into one corrupted NUL record, and `-exec false` short-circuits -print0 (rc 0, zero records, no diagnostic) -> rc 2 at buildArgv for any action word with print0 = 1. MAJORS: `--` ends the option list only and cannot rescue a start point (the first draft implied otherwise); `-exec CMD {} \;` failures leave rc 0 while `{} +` propagates (third named deviation); F9's cd must happen in the test file's own shell (a subshell fills the array where the assertion cannot see it and trips D6); a line-based sort destroys a newline name -> sort -z is the comparison primitive; an empty start point '' reached the tool (rc 1) -> rc 2. MINOR/NIT: type regex admits duplicates (tool rc 1, parity); depths emitted from $__KK_INT (`+1` verbatim is rc 1) and > INT_MAX is the tool's rc 1; -newer MISSING is fatal not partial (F8 split); a Windows start point survives as a prefix with `/` separators; -L + type=l matches only broken links; -quit/-prune/-delete are order-incompatible with the fixed action position; -name is case-sensitive on NTFS under msys; caller-side glob expansion keeps one word silently (README rule + case); -size +0 needs non-empty fixtures; bench 1.13x/1.16x on 400 files, worst single pairing 1.64x, date +%s%N costs ~20 ms; `[!-(]*` is a negated class; kt_make_symlink lives in tdirectory's helper; no permission-denied test is possible here. 20+ claims verified correct and listed in PLAN §8.

Owner: start tfind. GNU findutils 4.10.0 measured under both bashes: start points positional BEFORE the expression (the reverse of grep/head), -L only before them, `--` accepted, a start point beginning with `-` is an unknown predicate (rc 1), no start point = `.`, -maxdepth 08 decimal, 4.10 no longer warns about global-option order (the wrapper still emits them first), -type f,d works, -print splits a newline name while -print0 keeps it, an explicit action suppresses the implied -print, -exec works through argv, Windows paths accepted and echoed in their own spelling, rc 1 for every error with partial output kept. Decisions: no `--`, refuse ^[-!(] start points (rc 2), typed followSymlinks (addArg -L would land in the wrong position), print0 -> derived -0 with the P3-F1 guard (no header exception: find has no headers), depths via kk.isInt + >= 0 (no sign semantics here, unlike head/tail), TFind.byName PATTERN START... one-liner, and tutil._badOut turned into the TUTIL_OUT_PREFIXES registry instead of a fourth hard-coded edit. PLAN.md + this ledger written. No code.
